notes: Five things a formatter has to get right for Kazakh. FIRST, THE MONTH NAMES ARE NATIVE TURKIC AND PERSIAN, not Russian-derived: qantar, aqpan, nauryz, sauir and so on, never yanvar / fevral. This separates Kazakh from Azerbaijani, Uzbek and Kyrgyz-in-practice, all of which took the Russian set, and it is the single commonest way a Kazakh date comes out wrong. SECOND, monthsInDate is IDENTICAL to months and that is correct, not a copy-paste slip: the Kazakh month name does not change shape inside a date, so 5 qantar 2026 uses the plain nominative. What does change is the YEAR, which normally takes a suffix — 2026 jylgy 5 qantar, '5 January of the year 2026' — so a config building a full Kazakh date string needs the word jyl or jylgy, which no format token supplies. THIRD, month and weekday names are LOWER CASE, always, including at the start of a sentence-initial date. FOURTH, the weekday array here is Sunday-first because the formatter wants it that way, while date/weekday.txt in the pack is Monday-first because that is how a Kazakh calendar prints it; both are the same seven words. FIFTH, the numeric format is DD.MM.YYYY with dots and leading zeros, time is 24-hour with a colon and Kazakh has no am/pm, the decimal separator is a comma, the thousands separator is a space, and the tenge sign follows the number after a space: 1 234,56 tenge. The tenge replaced the rouble on 15 November 1993, which is a public holiday, so any monetary series crossing that date changes unit.
